summary: (b) The contentions of the Petitioner in the present Petition, which are contrary to/in the teeth of the findings rendered by this Commission in the order dated 30.12.2019, read with the order dated 6.12.2021, can never be termed as a “dispute” under Section 79(1)(f) of the Electricity Act, 2003. Once an issue has been decided by this Commission, any party seeking to act in a manner contrary to/in violation of the judgment can never contend that such conduct is a “dispute”, for seeking to invoke the jurisdiction of the Commission u/s 79(1)(f) of the 2003 Act. There is no “dispute” permitting the Petitioner to file the present Petition, which deserves to be rejected, at the threshold itself, on this ground as well. (g) From a bare perusal of the literal meaning of ‘dispute’, which means disagreement between the parties, the present issue squarely falls under the definition of dispute as provided under section 79 (1)(f) of the Act, and therefore, is triable by this Commission. Without prejudice to the above submissions, it is submitted that Order 7 Rule 11of the CPC lays down the guiding principles for rejection of any plaint or dismissal of any suit on maintainability. It is evident that there does not exist any ground for seeking rejection of the present Petition. Further, KSEBL and TANGEDCO have failed to establish any of the above conditions, which go to the root of the present matter and warrant its dismissal on maintainability itself. Therefore, in terms of above, it is evident that the present petition is maintainable, as the plain reading of the averment made in the Petition, would evince that there arises a cause of action, as soon as KSEBL has refused to honour the invoices dated 6.1.2022 raised in terms of Regulation 8(6) of the 2014 Tariff Regulations, and continues to subsist as same remains unpaid by KSEBL. Thus, the main thrust of KSEBL that there does not exist a cause of action to initiate the present proceedings as the same is barred by the principle of res judicata, is not based on the correct position of law and cannot be sustained. (h) The contentions raised by KSEBL are factual in nature, which requires a detailed hearing, and therefore the present Petition is liable to be heard on merits, as the action of non-honouring the invoices raised by the Petitioner, and re-agitating the same issue again and again to prolong the legitimate claim of the Petitioner, is unknown to settled judicial principles. It is a settled position of law that while considering whether the present Petition is maintainable or not, this Commission can only examine whether the present Petition _prima facie_ shows a cause of action, and there cannot be embarkment upon the veracity of the averments made in the Petition (Reliance placed on _D. Ramachandran v. R.V. Janakiraman_ (1999) 3 SCC _No Court shall try any suit or issue in which the matter directly and substantially in issue has been directly and substantially in issue in a former suit between the same parties, or between parties under whom they or any of them claim, litigating under the same title, in a Court competent to try such subsequent suit or the suit in which such issue has been subsequently raised, and has been heard and finally decided by such Court._ and substantially similar, the question of issue estoppel does not arise. In other words, while the principle of sharing of gains by the Petitioner, on a monthly basis with annual reconciliation in terms of Regulation 8(6) of the 2014 Tariff Regulations was laid down in the earlier orders, the question for consideration in the present Petition is whether the invoices raised by the Petitioner, is in accordance with the said regulations/ orders or not. Further, the contention of KSEBL that the present Petition is not maintainable as there does not exist any cause of action, is misconceived, since the cause of action in the present petition arose on 6.1.2022, when the invoices raised by the Petitioner, was not paid by the Respondents, thereby giving rise to a ‘dispute’ between the parties, which is required to be adjudicated under Section 79(1)(f) read with Section 79(1)(a) of the Act. For all the above reasons, we reject the submission of the Respondents and hold that the present Petition is maintainable. 33. We agree with the submissions of the Petitioner that the present petition is based on subsequent developments and the cause of action has arisen in the present petition only after raising the invoices dated 6.1.2022 by the Petitioner on the Respondents, which have been disputed by the Respondents. In order to address the dispute, the term “annual reconciliation”, as mentioned in our Order dated 30.12.2021, is required to be interpreted in the present set of facts.
title: Petition on behalf of NTPC Limited under Section 79(1)(f) of the Electricity Act, seeking directions against KSEBL and TANGEDCO for the release of the amount due and payable towards the Bills dated 6.1.2022, along with the Late Payment Surcharge. NTPC Limited
